title: 1954 AHSME Problem 36
statement: A boat has a speed of \(15\) mph in still water. In a stream that has a current of \(5\) mph it travels a certain distance downstream and returns. The ratio of the average speed for the round trip to the speed in still water is:

solutions.text:
For a one-way distance \(d,\) the total time is \[ \frac d{20}+\frac d{10}=\frac{3d}{20}. \] Thus the round-trip average speed is \[ \frac{2d}{\frac{3d}{20}}=\frac{40}{3}. \] Its ratio to \(15\) is \[ \frac{\frac{40}{3}}{15}=\frac89. \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The downstream and upstream speeds are \(20\) mph and \(10\) mph
For equal distances, divide twice the distance by \(\frac{d}{20}+\frac{d}{10}\)
